The renowned Chinese video blogger team "Film Hurricane" announced that it has joined Alibaba International, the world's largest B2B cross-border platform, and is fully leveraging AI to expand into overseas markets. It is reported that the team has already received cooperation inquiries from clients in over 30 countries.  

According to the team, they utilized multiple AI agents on Alibaba International to translate product information with one click, generate multilingual product descriptions and videos tailored for overseas markets, and quickly set up their international store. Their main products include T-shirts, hoodies, sportswear, and accessories, which are consistent with those sold on their domestic e-commerce platform.  

Additionally, when engaging with overseas clients, the Film Hurricane team extensively used the platform's AI agents to assist in customer service.

Según se informa, el equipo ya ha recibido expresiones de interés de colaboración de clientes en más de 30 países. Utilizando múltiples agentes de IA disponibles en Alibaba.com, el equipo ha traducido automáticamente la información de productos y generado descripciones multilingües y videos adaptados a los mercados internacionales, permitiendo la rápida apertura de su tienda en línea en el extranjero. Los productos principales en su tienda incluyen camisetas, sudaderas con capucha, ropa deportiva y accesorios, coincidiendo con los ofrecidos en su comercio electrónico nacional. On August 7, 2020, during the "Commemorating Thomas S. Huang—40 Years of Inheritance in Chinese Computer Vision" session at the Fifth GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit, Harry Shum, Yang Shiqiang, Chen Changwen, Zhang Zhengyou, Tian Qi, and Yan Shuicheng recounted the "40-year inheritance" as follows: In 2006, Thomas S. Huang attended a Christmas event organized by Quan Long in Hong Kong and coincidentally discovered that several leading figures in computer vision present were each a decade apart in age—Thomas S. Huang (born 1936), Ma Songde (born 1946), Gao Wen (born 1956), and Harry Shum (born 1966). Subsequently, they discussed whether they could find another leading figure in computer vision a decade younger at their next gathering. The discussion quickly pointed to the same person: Sun Jian (born 1976), Harry Shum's distinguished protégé. The protagonists of this story—Ma Songde, Gao Wen, Harry Shum, and Sun Jian—are also regular attendees of past GAIR summits, gathering there due to inheritance and evangelism. Each time they see young people in the GAIR audience with tears in their eyes or young scholars writing in live-stream comments, "This is what I aspire to become," they are filled with anticipation, waiting for these young people, both on-site and behind screens, to take up the torch of inheritance.
